pursuitCity: I am following a person, not collecting destinations. The distinction should appear in the expenses.
A fugitive can change cities. Unfortunately, so can I.
I should establish what the trail actually says before adding another place to it.
The local population has not been briefed on how helpful I would like them to be.
An ordinary day for everyone else. I should introduce the investigation gently.
I need useful information. Enthusiastic directions to a good lunch remain a separate category.
I should check the description before asking whether anyone has seen "someone suspicious".
Travelling for work sounds better before the work starts travelling ahead of you.
The map offers possibilities. It has declined to take responsibility for my choice.
A useful question can save a journey. I should have several ready.
I should write down the answer before memory improves its dramatic structure.
Someone may have noticed something. My task is to make that sentence less vague.
A convincing story travels well. That is precisely why I should check it.
I can look like I belong here or ask for directions. Ideally both, but the timing is delicate.
Another conversation might help. Preferably one in which I do more listening than demonstrating my theory.
The chase needs evidence. My growing expertise in arrival procedures is not enough.

contact: A possible source. I should begin with a question, not the entire history of my journey.
They may know something useful. Best not start by explaining what that must be.
I need to distinguish what they saw from what somebody else told them.
An ordinary conversation, with an unusually specific interest in somebody else's travel arrangements.
I should have the details ready. "Recently" is a large period when somebody is trying to remember.
People notice different things. I should not reject a useful answer because it arrived with an anecdote.
The most useful person is not always the one who looks pleased to see me.
I should let the answer finish before deciding which part belongs in my notes.
revisitedContact: I have been here before. I should review the earlier answer before ordering another one.
A repeat visit needs a reason. "I forgot to listen" is honest but not ideal.
Best compare my notes before asking somebody to reproduce their memory on demand.
I should check whether I have a new question or merely renewed optimism.
An answer does not become independent confirmation because I hear it twice.
I can revisit the conversation. I should avoid bringing exactly the same confusion.
place: A place to investigate. What it might tell me depends on what is actually here.
I should arrive with a question and leave with something more precise than an impression.
A promising stop. The promise is mine; the place has made no commitments.
Best observe before deciding which detail is important.
I should not confuse an interesting location with a relevant one.
An address can be a lead without being the answer.
hotel: A hotel. Somewhere to stop moving without calling off the investigation.
Rest might improve my judgement. Continuing until I agree with every theory probably will not.
I should weigh the rest against the remaining time. Both require attention.
A temporary base. Ideally, I will leave it with the same case and a clearer head.
I can review the notes after recovering. They are unlikely to flee independently.
A room is not progress, but being able to think may contribute to some.
shop: Supplies should support the chase. I do not need to furnish the journey.
I should check my inventory before giving the same problem a second receipt.
The useful purchase is the one I need, not the one with the most reassuring packaging.
A shopkeeper can sell me supplies. A reliable next destination remains my responsibility.
I should decide what is missing before browsing for things to miss.
I am here to follow a trail, not create one made entirely of purchases.
destinations: The next destination should come from the clues, not my preference for the name.
I should compare the descriptions before committing to another journey.
A ticket makes a decision official. It does not make it correct.
If two places seem to fit, I should find out what distinguishes them.
The route needs a reason I can explain without waving at the map.
A confident departure is still a departure. Best make it an informed one.

arrived: Arrived. I should find out what this place can tell me before deciding what it proves.
New stop. Same case. Best keep those facts connected.
I have reached the city. Reaching a conclusion will require a separate effort.
First, check the available leads. Looking purposeful can continue during the process.
Here I am. The investigation would appreciate knowing what I intend to do next.
newTravelClue: A new detail about the route. I should record the exact wording before it becomes a destination in my head.
That may help narrow the options. "May" is doing useful work in that sentence.
A travel clue. Best compare it with the other information rather than immediately with the booking options.
I have something new to work with. I should check what it rules out as well as what it suggests.
The route is becoming more specific. My interpretation should not become more specific than the clue.
conflictingClues: The clues point in different directions. I need to resolve that before paying to demonstrate it.
Two incompatible accounts. I should establish whether they describe the same part of the journey.
I may have misunderstood a detail. That is cheaper to check here than after departure.
The information does not agree. Choosing the more convenient version is not a method.
I need a distinction, not a favourite. Best review the clues together.
deadEndConfirmed: This lead has not held up. I should return to the last supported part of the route.
A dead end. Useful to recognise before I build an itinerary around it.
I need to correct the route, not defend the money already spent following it.
That direction did not produce the trail I needed. Back to what I can actually support.
A wrong turn is information. Repeating it would be a preference.
locationClosed: Closed. An exceptionally clear answer to a question I had not intended to ask.
I should check the opening hours. Knocking with greater conviction is not a scheduling tool.
The place is closed. I can plan another stop instead of examining the entrance professionally.
A closed location is not concealing evidence merely by having business hours.
I need to compare waiting with the other available leads. The door is unlikely to advise me.
departureReady: The next stop has support. I should check the destination once more before confirming the journey.
I have enough to choose the next destination. Best take the reasoning with me.
Time to move on. Ideally without leaving the useful part of the investigation in my notes here.
The route is ready for another step. Not an invitation to skip the next questions.
I should finish checking the travel details. A near match is an expensive way to describe a ticket.
lowEnergy: I am beginning to mistake movement for progress. Rest deserves consideration.
My concentration is travelling separately. I need it back before the next decision.
I should recover before I start agreeing with the last person who spoke.
Tiredness makes every destination sound equally plausible. An unhelpful talent.
A short assessment of my options would help. Provided I can finish remembering the options.
timeRunningLow: The remaining time needs a plan, not a motivational speech.
I need the most useful next step. Visiting everything is no longer even an attractive bad idea.
The deadline is close. I should cut unnecessary detours, not necessary checks.
Time is short. My reasoning should become more focused, not more imaginative.
I should review what remains unresolved before spending more time confirming what I already know.
warrantMissing: I still need the warrant. A convincing journey does not authorise an arrest.
The paperwork needs to catch up before I try to catch anyone else.
I should complete the warrant before relying on handcuffs to introduce the subject.
An arrest needs the proper warrant. My travel history is not an acceptable substitute.
I have followed the case this far. Best not lose it to a preventable omission on a form.
finalIdentificationReady: Time to identify the suspect. The description matters more than who looks suitably guilty.
I need the person supported by the evidence, not the face that would improve the story.
The identification deserves one careful comparison. Familiarity is not a distinguishing feature.
I should check the recorded details before committing to a face.
The journey has brought me to this choice. It has not made the choice on my behalf.
